a_restatement: The thread describes AI memory systems as a specific technical architecture: memory objects are extracted from user interactions and stored with metadata in a datastore, not a transcript.

When queried, the system retrieves relevant memories by comparing query embeddings to stored objects, keeps the highest-scoring subset by relevance, and allows memories to be corrected, merged, or refined as new information arrives.
Users can request explicit forgetting or schedule automatic deletion after a set period, and the system uses these memories to inform both what the agent says and what actions it performs.

b_answers.answer: A model predicts what is worth remembering and extracts it from cached inputs.
b_answers.quoted_span: A model decides what to store: cached inputs go to the model system, which predicts what is worth remembering and extracts it.

b_answers.answer: It is stored as a memory value in a memory object, which also contains metadata such as timestamp, trigger, and interaction summary.
b_answers.quoted_span: It is stored as a memory value in a memory object, and one trigger is you asking the agent to remember your favorite architect.

b_answers.answer: The system scores stored memory objects for relevance by comparing query embeddings to memory value embeddings using cosine similarity, keeps the top subset, and orders them by timestamp.
b_answers.quoted_span: Instead of rereading your whole history, the agent scores stored memory objects for relevance to your query. It compares a query embedding to memory value embeddings by a measure such as cosine similarity, keeps a top subset, and orders them by timestamp.

b_answers.answer: The system deletes the specified information when given the command.
b_answers.quoted_span: Forgetting is claimed: "forget that" deletes the specified information

b_answers.answer: The system queues it for deletion, and a maintenance cycle automatically deletes objects past their expiration time.
b_answers.quoted_span: "forget this after three months" queues it for deletion. A maintenance cycle deletes objects past their expiration time on its own

b_answers.answer: The older memory object is replaced or updated with the new information. Aligned objects can merge, and values are refined by contradicting input rather than overwritten.
b_answers.quoted_span: Memories are corrected: new timestamped input is matched to the prior memory object it concerns, which is then replaced or updated. Aligned objects can merge, and a value kept with supporting interactions is refined by contradicting input, not overwritten.

b_answers.answer: The problem is that agents forget, requiring users to re-enter details repeatedly. What is different is the described technical architecture with memory objects from interactions, retrieved by relevance, corrected over time, and deletable on request.
b_answers.quoted_span: When an AI agent says it "remembers" you, is that architecture or marketing? Agents forget, so you re-enter the same details; the claim is a loop — query plus memory data from a datastore of your past interactions, into a sequence model, out as a response.
